english: If it rains, the ground gets wet. It's raining, so the ground is wet.
note: 'gets wet' and 'is wet' are the same claim reworded

english: If the alarm had gone off, the neighbours would have heard it. The neighbours didn't hear anything, so the alarm didn't go off.
If you don't charge your phone, it'll die before lunch. You didn't charge it, so it's going to die before lunch.
note: The claim is 'you charge your phone', negated, never a separate letter for not charging it

english: If the shop's open and I've got cash, I'll buy milk. The shop is open. I've got cash too, so I'm buying milk.
The dog barks if someone knocks. Someone knocked, so the dog barked.
note: Letters go by first appearance, so the consequent is X

english: My plants die if I forget to water them. I forgot to water them this week, so they're going to die.
You get a refund if you return it within 30 days. You didn't get a refund, so you can't have returned it within 30 days.
You can vote only if you're registered. You can vote, so you must be registered.
note: 'A only if B' is A→B, not B→A

english: I'll pass the exam only if I study. I'm not going to study, so I won't pass.
Whenever it snows, the buses run late. It snowed this morning, so the buses were late.
Whenever I open a can of tuna the cat comes running. The cat didn't come running, so I didn't open any tuna.
I get a headache whenever I skip breakfast. I skipped breakfast today, so I'm going to get a headache.
note: 'B whenever A', with the consequent first
